key_concepts: Plants reproduce through several modes, including asexual reproduction.
Common plant propagation methods are cutting, budding, layering, and grafting.
Cutting uses a healthy stem or leaf portion to grow roots and form a new plant.
Budding can be done through a T-budding technique.
Rootstock and scion are terms used in budding and grafting.
Asexual propagation can use stem cuttings, leaf cuttings, or plantlets.
Plant propagation is important in agriculture, horticulture, and environmental conservatio
Propagation helps produce more plants with desirable traits.
Scientific investigations need fair tests, replication, and accurate measurement.
Lagundi (Vitex negundo) is an example of a plant propagated by cutting.
